note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Benchmark construction through LLM evaluation, user studies, and evaluator reliability

nodes.name: Experimental design needs expertise
nodes.description: Designing experiments and selecting experimental settings in empirical science is challenging and requires significant domain expertise; scientists often learn of missing ablations only after peer review.

nodes.name: ABGEN is the first ablation-design benchmark
nodes.description: ABGEN is the first benchmark evaluating LLMs on designing ablation studies, with 1,500 expert-annotated examples derived from 807 NLP papers.

nodes.name: Task definition
nodes.description: Given an expert-restructured research context (background, methodology, main experiment setup and results) and a module name, the LLM must generate a research objective and detailed experimental process for an ablation of that module.

nodes.name: Paper filtering criteria
nodes.description: Papers that are not experimental or have fewer than two ablation studies are excluded; 807 papers remain after filtering.

nodes.name: Three evaluation criteria
nodes.description: Ablation designs are rated 1-5 on importance, faithfulness to the research context, and soundness.

nodes.name: Annotators agree substantially
nodes.description: Inter-annotator Cohen's Kappa is 0.735 for importance, 0.782 for faithfulness and 0.710 for soundness.

nodes.name: Best LLM trails human experts
nodes.description: Even the best LLM, DeepSeek-R1-0528, performs much worse than human experts on importance, faithfulness and soundness.

nodes.name: Automated and human evaluation disagree
nodes.description: Despite similar LLM-based evaluation scores to o4-mini, DeepSeek-R1-0528 outperforms it on every criterion in human evaluation, suggesting automated evaluation is unreliable here.

nodes.name: Five common error types
nodes.description: Error analysis of 100 failure cases (average human score below 3) finds five error types: misalignment with research context, ambiguity and difficulty in reproduction, partial or incomplete ablation, insignificant ablation module, and inherent logical inconsistencies.

nodes.name: Researcher feedback improves LLM designs
nodes.description: On 20 failure cases each, expert feedback of at most 50 words lets GPT-4o improve to 4.8/4.2/4.6 (+0.9/+2.1/+2.6) and Llama-3.1-70B to 4.5/3.9/4.1 on importance/faithfulness/soundness.

nodes.name: Findings generalize to other domains
nodes.description: User studies in biomedical sciences and computer networks (27 examples over ten papers) give human scores consistent with the NLP domain.

nodes.name: ABGEN-EVAL meta-evaluation benchmark
nodes.description: ABGEN-EVAL contains 1,800 examples (18 LLM outputs x 100 human assessments) built from the human assessments to meta-evaluate automated evaluators.

nodes.name: LLM judges correlate poorly with humans
nodes.description: Instance-level and system-level correlations of LLM-based evaluators with human judgments are relatively low, so current automated evaluation is not reliable for ablation designs.

isolated_nodes.name: Reference ablation has three parts
isolated_nodes.description: Each reference ablation study consists of a research objective, an experiment process and a result discussion; LLMs are not required to generate the result discussion.

isolated_nodes.name: Generation setup
isolated_nodes.description: All LLM generation experiments use temperature 1.0 and a maximum output length of 1024 tokens, since the longest reference ablation study is 518 words.

isolated_nodes.name: Evaluator setup
isolated_nodes.description: The base automated evaluator is GPT-4.1-mini, given the research context and reference ablation, scoring each criterion separately after generating a rationale.

structural_reasoning: Linear pipeline: motivation, benchmark construction, evaluation, analysis, user studies and meta-evaluation of automated judges.
